markingScheme.criterion: Quotes at least two of the student's own logged Strength Dial readings (a strength setting with its skin damage percentage or the hazard label it needed) as evidence.
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine strength/damage or strength/label pairs from the student's own Investigation Record rows; exact wording not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim ('stronger is worse') with no actual logged readings quoted.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains that as the acid was made stronger (more concentrated) the damage to the skin sample increased, so the label needed moved from low hazard to irritant (exclamation mark) to corrosive.
markingScheme.accept: Any valid phrasing linking higher strength/concentration to more damage and a more serious hazard label.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only 'the damage changed' or 'it got dangerous' with no link to strength or label.

markingScheme.criterion: States, from the alkali (sodium hydroxide) readings, that an alkali also became corrosive at high strength, so both acids and alkalis can be corrosive or irritant depending on strength.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct statement that alkalis can be as hazardous as acids and depend on strength too.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only 'alkalis are different' or 'alkalis are safe'.

markingScheme.criterion: Expects the corrosive hazard symbol (liquid dripping onto a hand and a surface) because concentrated hydrochloric acid damages skin, eyes and materials.
markingScheme.accept: Any description of the corrosive pictogram with a reason about burns/damage to skin or eyes.
markingScheme.insufficient: Naming the exclamation-mark or flame symbol, or naming the symbol with no reason.

markingScheme.criterion: Names at least two sensible pieces of PPE (safety goggles, gloves, lab coat/apron, closed shoes) and links each to the part of the body a splash could reach.
markingScheme.accept: Any two correct items each with a protective reason, e.g. goggles protect the eyes, gloves protect the hands.
markingScheme.insufficient: Listing PPE items with no reason, or only one item.

markingScheme.criterion: States the immediate first aid: rinse the affected skin at once with plenty of cold running water (for a long time) and tell the teacher/an adult.
markingScheme.accept: Wash/flood/rinse with lots of water straight away plus telling a teacher or adult; mention of at least 10 minutes is a bonus, not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: Waiting, wiping with a cloth, rubbing, or adding another chemical.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply). Award marks point-by-point using each question's marking_scheme in marking_context: each point is worth the marks stated and is independent unless it names a dependsOn point; each point's 'accept'/'insufficient' tell you exactly what does and doesn't count. use_of_evidence's 3 marks ARE the Explain marking_scheme's 3 points, and reasoning's 3 marks ARE the Apply marking_scheme's 3 points - the rubric levels restate the same points as bands; award each set of 3 marks ONCE, not twice. communication is a separate, holistic 2 marks across both answers' clarity and vocabulary, never overlapping with the content marks. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy (8 marks = full). Use the student's own logged Investigation Record (station/setting/reading/outcome columns in simulation_results.trials, especially the Strength Dial rows with strength and skin damage percentage) to check that any claim about their own readings is consistent with what they actually did. Accept scientifically valid alternative wording and do not penalise spelling unless meaning is unclear. Total is out of 16 (8 auto + 3 + 3 + 2); report the percentage, one strength, one correction, and one next step, in under 80 words.
